summary: A 65-foot Aermotor lookout tower from the late 1950s in Rhea County, Tennessee. The cab is locked; its condition and use after 2019 are unconfirmed.

facts.design: 65-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 ft cab, built in the late 1950s (no exact year in the sources read)

access.note: Cab is locked. The register says signage allows visitors to climb at their own risk; the sources read do not confirm the site's owner or current use.

evidence.quote: This 65-foot Aermotor tower was built in the late 1950s and features a 7'x7' cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Eastern US Lookouts page title is spelled 'Smryna'; the register and the state list use 'Smyrna'. Treated as a typo.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, multiple property document

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register gives only 'late 1950s' for construction, so no built event was written. The brief's 2019 NHLR registration was not seen in the pages read, so it is not cited. Topozone (search snippet only, not read) places the tower on an 'Evensville' USGS map, a possible place-name variant. A 2015 TDF tower history report (search snippet only, not read) probably gives the exact build year. The NRHP study's county table appears to list a Smyrna entry in Rhea County (table layout not quoted). Staffing and any status after 2019 are unknown. Page reads for this tower reached the six-read budget.
